## Claims
- [source-backed] Reiner–Woo–Yong, arXiv:0809.2981v2, state that the outside-box Schur classes form an ideal \(I_{r,n-r}\), induce \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\), and that \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. [source-2, lines 1320-1330]
- [source-backed] For a bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), Bruhat comparison among \(r\)-Grassmannian permutations is partition inclusion; consequently \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2, lines 1354-1375]
- [source-backed] Theorem 5.4 is integral: for a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), it gives two ideal-generating families in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2, lines 1380-1401]
- [source-backed] The source retains the project’s trajectory: minimality of both Theorem 5.4 families is explicitly conjectural, while the stronger assertion \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is stated only as suspected. [source-2, lines 1495-1502; source-2, lines 1517-1552]
- [unsupported] The retrieved external-provider candidates contain no exact theorem text relevant to Grassmannian box quotients or integral Schur spans; the arXiv candidates identified concern path integrals or trajectory-data mining, not Schubert calculus. [arxiv:2112.15391v3; arxiv:2403.14151v2]
- [unsupported] The supplied primary-source locator proves ideal generation by the containing-box Schur classes, but does not itself explicitly state the stronger equality \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). Establishing that equality still requires an integral multiplication-closure argument (for example via Littlewood–Richardson multiplication).

## Strategy
Use arXiv:0809.2981v2 as the citable grounding for the quotient \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), its integral box-Schur basis, and ideal generation of \(J_v\), with \(q=n-r\). Retain the Schur-span equality as a separately required integral lemma.

## Gaps
No retrieved external theorem with exact text replaces the missing integral Schur-span equality or the auxiliary polynomial presentation
\[
\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}).
\]
The bounded provider search was incomplete: Semantic Scholar failed with HTTP 429.

## Next
Cite source-2, lines 1320-1330 and 1354-1375 for the box quotient and ideal-generating description. Separately prove or locate an exact integral Littlewood–Richardson closure statement before treating the Schur-span formulation as source-grounded.
